title: MBD Establishment Workshop
subtitle: A reusable workshop story for moving from hand code to model-based design
audience: System and software engineers evaluating how to establish an MBD workflow from existing embedded C code.
purpose: Reframe the source workshop into a clear training flow that shows why generic conversion steps are insufficient, what artifacts must be inspected, and how a repeatable MBD establishment path works.
coverTalkTrack: This workshop is about turning an existing hand-code workflow into a repeatable model-based design establishment process. The deck is organized around decisions and artifacts, not around copying every original slide.
sourceFacts: The source deck is a 61-slide MBD establishment workshop created from a customer-safe example.
The original story starts with generic hand-code-to-MBD steps, then shows why those steps need real project inputs.
The source workshop repeatedly reviews the path: define scope, analyze workflow and software architecture, convert typical software components, convert architecture, test, and plan next steps.
Source evidence includes C code excerpts, type/data definitions, software component boundaries, workflow diagrams, and a final next-step discussion.
missingInputs: Replace generated placeholders with project-safe screenshots or exported model views if this becomes a customer-ready deck.

slides.reason: Set the story around artifact-driven decisions instead of a list of topics.
slides.talkTrack: We start with the problem: the usual conversion checklist sounds reasonable, but it does not tell us what to do with real project constraints. The rest of the workshop shows how source code, architecture, workflow, and test evidence drive the conversion decisions.

slides.title: Reusable MBD establishment pattern
slides.subtitle: Takeaways for the audience
items: Start from project evidence, not from a generic conversion checklist.
Use System Composer after boundaries and interfaces are justified by artifacts.
Use Simulink, requirements, and tests to make the conversion reviewable.
Track missing screenshots, data, and assumptions as explicit gaps.
slides.reason: Close the training loop with a memorable reusable method.
slides.talkTrack: The reusable pattern is evidence first, architecture second, behavior third, verification always. Missing information is not ignored; it is tracked as a project gap.
builds: Reveal the four takeaways in order.
